source: Lin, Li, Wang, Douglas, Golani, Chheda (2026) Clarification Is Not Correction: LLMs Fail to Let Go
finding: Gap 8 and 1. Early ambiguous turns harden into one hidden task state; a later explicit clarification is treated as a patch, not a correction. Old-hypothesis residue stays in the output. Coding is worst. Summaries, chain of thought and a single-state ledger do not fix it.
numbers: Gemini-2.5-Pro and Flash, thousands of trials. Success full/clarified-first/ambiguous-first: Pro 54.2/50.0/42.8, Flash 62.3/55.4/45.7. In ambiguous-first: writing 69.3% success (contamination 0.125), planning 37.5% (0.141), coding 24.4% (0.256). Baselines success/contamination: raw history 43.2/0.177, summary memory 48.7/0.228, CoT 44.3/0.182, single-state ledger 44.6/0.295. 62.5% of summaries collapsed the ambiguity, 37.5% kept it.
quote: later clarification is often treated as additional context rather than as a corrective signal
limits: Only two Gemini models; contamination metric is lexical/semantic and partly overlaps recency bias; authors say they do not separate stale state from all order effects. Preprint, Meta authors.
agent_relevance: A summary or one-slot ledger of the frame is not enough. The ledger must carry epistemic status (confirmed, tentative, contradicted). Code-heavy tasks need extra care because the early frame gets baked into structure.

source: Lin et al. (2026) Clarification Is Not Correction, appendix C: K-hypothesis ablation and naive multi-hypothesis prompting
finding: Gap 1. Simply listing more hypotheses does not help reliably. It helped one model and hurt the other. Naive multi-hypothesis prompting gave the highest contamination of all methods.
numbers: Success at K=1/3/5 hypotheses: Gemini-2.5-Pro 4.7/10.7/19.1; Gemini-2.5-Flash 22.6/5.8/5.0. Mean contamination: multi-hypothesis 1.029 vs raw history 0.177, summary 0.228, CoT 0.182, single-state ledger 0.295 (score-2 share 11.2% vs 1.2% for raw history).
limits: Supplementary negative control, small setting, not token matched, not on puzzle tasks. Success levels are very low (4.7% to 22.6%).
agent_relevance: This is the closest direct test of 'keep 2 to 3 frames' on an LLM. Result: unreliable and model dependent without arbitration. If S2 holds rival frames it needs a code step that scores and discards them, not just a longer list.

source: Lin et al. (2026) Clarification Is Not Correction: rollback and response-policy interventions
finding: Gap 8, 4. Telling the model to discard earlier assumptions and rebuild from the clarified requirement helped. A two-phase policy (resolve ambiguity first, then execute and regenerate) removed wrong commitment and contamination in a small test. Asking first removed wrong commitment but left some residue.
numbers: Normal clarification success 17.5%, contamination 0.100; explicit rollback 27.5%, contamination 0.000. Policies (committed wrong %, contamination): direct 40.0/1.20; list assumptions 27.3/0.82; ask first 0.0/0.40; two phase 0.0/0.00.
limits: Tiny supplementary sample, prompt-level rollback only; authors warn it is not a general fix. Does not test the never-abstain rule (G6).
agent_relevance: Supports a fresh rebuild after an O8 reframe rather than patching the old answer (consistent with G4). Suggests a code-forced 'ask for the missing cue first' step works against wrong commitment, but residue needs a regenerate step.

source: Preprint (2026) When Agents Commit Too Soon: Diagnosing Premature Commitment in LLM Agents (COLM 2026 workshop)
finding: Gap 4, 9. Hidden-state similarity across repeated runs at step 4 predicts how stable a ReAct agent's whole trajectory is, but it measures stability, not correctness. A 'commitment' prompt reduced variability against a token-matched filler but not against the plain agent, and did not raise accuracy.
numbers: Llama-3.1-70B, ReAct, HotpotQA, 100 questions x 10 runs, T=0.5. Step-4 similarity vs trajectory variability r = -0.35. Replicated on two other models and StrategyQA. Monitor from 3 partial runs: mean AUROC 0.81. Behavioural CV control 0.112, filler 0.132, commitment 0.095; vs filler -28% (d=0.33, Holm p=.003); vs control -15% (Holm p=.088, n.s.). Accuracy 0.923/0.902/0.908 (n.s.). Result disappears on hard questions; correct and confidently wrong questions overlap.
limits: Open-weight model, QA only. Authors say it cannot show that commitment was premature.
agent_relevance: Run-to-run agreement is not a sign of a right frame. A stable wrong frame looks the same as a stable right one, so agreement across samples should not be the reframe trigger or the stop test.

source: Ho, Wang, Peng, Jojic, Laban, Galley, Gao, Qin (2026) Agentic Conversation Context Curation (AC3), Table 1
finding: Gap 3. A separate analyzer that rebuilds the task specification from the user's messages only (outside the assistant's own turns), then resets the context, recovers most of the Lost-in-Conversation loss. This is a code-held, user-only ledger of cues. It worked on code and database tasks too.
numbers: GPT-5-mini, replay of difficulty-selected Lost-in-Conversation instances, accuracy %: baseline full context math 60.0, code 15.8, database 32.0, actions 82.6. Assistant omission (AO) 85.0, 73.7, 32.0, 47.8. Gated Reset (mean of 3 runs) math 80.0 (closes 80% of the 25.0pp gap to AO), code 64.4 (closes 84% of 57.9pp), database 38.7 (above AO), actions closes 55% of its gap. Math gain is confounded: 47% of analyzer outputs contained the answer.
limits: Instances picked for difficulty, so absolute levels are low and regression to the mean is possible (authors also ran unselected pools, see d06). On tau2-bench with tool results in assistant turns, AO collapses to 0% and no AC3 operator beats full context. Preprint.
agent_relevance: Direct support for a code-held cue ledger built from user and environment evidence only. A model recap of its own history is the weak option. Works where facts live in user turns; fails when facts live only in assistant or tool outputs, so the ledger must also store tool results.

source: Ho et al. (2026) AC3, unselected pools and summarisation controls
finding: Gap 3. On full unselected pools, resetting from a rebuilt spec beats full context, and a faithful LLM summary does not. The summariser did not flag a single assistant error, so it carried wrong reasoning forward.
numbers: LiC database, n=107, gpt-5.4-mini: full context 56.1%, AO 69.2%, Concat User 63.6%, Reset 75.7% (+19.6pp, p=0.0005); condenser 53.3% at one call per turn (-2.8pp, p=0.68) and 47.7% at two calls (-8.4pp, p=0.08). Code pool n=100: full 83.0%, Reset 92.0% (+9.0pp, McNemar p=0.023). Condenser flagged an assistant error in 0 of 340 summaries. 'Pollution is contagious': an analyzer that sees the assistant's reasoning can do worse than no intervention.
limits: Main runs use GPT-5 family respondents; WildChat preferences come from one GPT-5-mini judge; CollabLLM results mixed.
agent_relevance: Answers whether a model recap cures fixation: no, a user-only rebuild does. Keep the model's earlier reasoning out of the context that builds the new frame. Reasoning-model coverage is partial.

source: Liu, Zhu, Feng, Ma, Wang, Meng (2026) Intent Mismatch Causes LLMs to Get Lost in Multi-Turn Conversation
finding: Gap 3, 7. A Mediator that rewrites vague user input into explicit instructions recovers much of the multi-turn loss. Plain summaries and a memory store (Mem0) barely help. Even a reasoning model (DeepSeek-v3.2-Thinking) stays hurt without the rewrite.
numbers: GPT-4o-mini, four task domains (C, D, A, M): Full 86.9 average, Sharded 53.6, +Summary 54.7, +Mem0 56.5, +Mediator 73.9 (C 51.4 to 66.9; D 52.5 to 65.3; A 45.5 to 85.7; M 64.9 to 77.7). Average recovery about 20 points performance and 15 points reliability across backbones; DeepSeek-v3.2-Thinking +21.1. An in-context-learning variant matched accuracy at 3.6x tokens.
limits: Mediator uses historical interaction experience (few-shot guidelines), so it needs prior trajectories. Preprint. Not a test of neutral rewording of a task statement in general.
agent_relevance: Restating intent into a clean explicit spec (an S1 hygiene step) is a strong lever on conversational input at modest token cost. Evidence is for rewriting user intent, not for neutral rewording of any input.

source: Fang et al. (2026) Benchmarking Multi-turn Medical Diagnosis: Hold, Lure, and Self-Correction (MINT)
finding: Gap 2, 4. Models rush to answer. When they delay and then revise, wrong-to-right revisions greatly outnumber right-to-wrong flips, so revision is net helpful once more evidence arrives. Withholding the diagnostic question until the end helps. Lab results act as lures.
numbers: 1,035 cases, 11 LLMs. Over 55.3% of first answers in the first two turns; 18.5% of those wrong. Incorrect-to-correct revisions up to 10.6x the rate of correct-to-incorrect flips (commercial models). Question-last beats question-first initial answer by 20.1% on average. Deferring the question raises first-commitment accuracy by up to 62.6%; reserving salient evidence for later prevents a drop of up to 23.3%. Guess rate 99.9% for Med42-70B vs 5.9% GPT-5-mini and 3.7% Claude Sonnet 4.6.
limits: Medical multiple choice; revision happens when new evidence arrives, not blind self-review. The ratio is per model and the headline is a maximum.
agent_relevance: Resolves the tension with Huang 2024: revision pays when new evidence arrives and hurts when it is blind self-review. The reframe trigger should be new cue or located failure, with a hold-before-commit option. Conflicts with G6 only if hold means abstain; here holding means asking for more cues, then answering.

source: Nikeghbal et al. (2026) Who Flips? Self- and Cross-Model Counterarguments Reveal Answer Instability in LLMs (MaxFlip)
finding: Gap 2. Gives a false-revision rate: how often a model abandons a correct answer when handed a coherent argument for a wrong option, with no social pressure.
numbers: Seven frontier models, 57 MMLU subjects. Flip rates 17.5% (Qwen3.5-35B) to 97.3% (Llama-3.1-8B); mean 48.7%, rising to 55.7% when the argument is attributed to the model itself (+7.1pp mean, up to +18.7pp). GPT-5.1 23.4%, Gemma-4-26B 23.0%, Qwen3.5-9B 39.3%, Llama-3.3-70B 75.8%. Flips vary by subject from 20.9% to 80.8%. Cross-model pooled best argument raises flips by up to +23.6pp (MaxFlip).
limits: Multiple choice with a built wrong argument; not a reframe trigger test. Flip is measured only on initially correct answers.
agent_relevance: A cue-conflict detector that hands the model a plausible rival story will produce false reframes at about 20 to 100% depending on the model. Any O8 trigger fed by model-written counter-arguments needs a code or tool check before the flip is accepted.

source: Naeini, Saqur, Saeidi, Giorgi, Taati (2023) Large Language Models are Fixated by Red Herrings: Only Connect Wall dataset
finding: Gap 10 (puzzle setting). Puzzle walls with deliberate red herrings (16 clues, 4 groups). Removing the red herrings raises solve counts sharply, a clean fixation signal. More few-shot examples did not help.
numbers: Test set 494 walls. Human performance about 80% correct connections. GPT-4 10-shot solved 6 of 494 walls (239 correct groups); on the randomised version (red herrings removed) 59 walls (595 groups); on the WordNet version 471 walls (1,926 groups). GPT-3.5 0-shot 0 walls vs 5 randomised vs 337 WordNet. Best connection F1 41-45% vs human about 80%.
limits: 2023 models (GPT-3.5/4), no reasoning models, no multi-turn. The synthetic datasets differ in more than red herrings.
agent_relevance: Shows the pattern: a strong prior frame pulled by distractor cues, which a reframe step must break. Also warns that more examples do not fix it. A re-test with current reasoning models is missing.

source: Chen, Zhu, Huang, Wang (2026) MedEinst: Benchmarking the Einstellung Effect in Medical LLMs
finding: Gap 10, 1. Paired control and trap cases show that accurate LLMs still follow the common diagnosis when one key discriminating cue is changed. An agent that forces explicit discriminative evidence checks cut the trap rate somewhat.
numbers: 5,383 paired cases, 49 diseases, 17 LLMs. GPT-5 failure types in error cases: blindness (key evidence ignored) over 35%; of cases where the cue was noticed, 43% underthinking and 22% overthinking (rationalising the prior). Qwen3-32B ablation (base acc / robust acc / trap rate): base 40.25/11.86/43.46; with dynamic causal inference 55.49/19.94/38.32; full agent 69.49/24.21/33.75.
limits: Medical; one agent design by the benchmark authors; the main table is garbled in text extraction, so only the ablation was read cleanly. Preprint.
agent_relevance: Strong models fail by ignoring one key cue, not by missing knowledge. Supports a forced step that asks which cue would separate rival frames and then checks it. The trap rate stayed at a third even with the agent.

source: Kim et al. (2025) Limitations of LLMs in Clinical Problem-Solving Arising from Inflexible Reasoning (M-ARC)
finding: Gap 10. Items built to trigger Einstellung (fixation from past experience) were failed by most LLMs in early 2025.
numbers: mARC about 100 items; physician mean about 66% (5 physicians); most LLMs under 50%, several near or below 20% chance; Gemini 1.5 Pro 50% and o1 48%; LLMs were also overconfident.
limits: Early-2025 models; small item set; physician N=5.
agent_relevance: Baseline against which later reasoning-model gains (d13) should be read.

source: Shidara et al. (2026) Advances in LLM Reasoning Enable Flexibility in Clinical Problem-Solving
finding: Gap 10. Newer reasoning models reach physician-level scores on the same Einstellung trap set. Reasoning helps on single-shot fixation tasks.
numbers: mARC: physicians mean 0.66 (95% CI 0.55-0.75; 5 physicians). Best model Claude 4.1 Opus 0.75 (CI 0.74-0.76); 15 runs per model. On the 20 items physicians most often missed (physician accuracy 36%), the top 5 models answered 55-70% correctly with high confidence; Claude 4.1 Opus decisively correct on 55.0%, decisively wrong on 25.0%.
limits: Single small benchmark, N=5 physicians, no code or puzzle task. Fixation is single-shot, not sequential, so it does not conflict with the multi-turn results.
agent_relevance: Single-shot anchoring is partly cured by reasoning; sequential fixation (d05, Laban 2025) is not. Our scaffold should aim at the sequential case.

source: Barber, Young, Coombe, Browne (2025) Solomonoff-Inspired Hypothesis Ranking with LLMs for Prediction Under Uncertainty
finding: Gap 1, 10. On Mini-ARC tasks, GPT-4 generates several hypotheses, which are weighted by simplicity and fit and mixed per cell. A tiny demonstration of multi-hypothesis on grid puzzles.
numbers: Task A (alternating column shifts, six hypotheses): Solomonoff-weighted 64% vs Bayesian model averaging 48%. Task B: both 100%. Task C with 20 noisy hypotheses: Solomonoff 60%, BMA 64%.
limits: Three hand-picked tasks, no single-hypothesis baseline, no equal-token comparison. Not evidence that multiple beats one.
agent_relevance: Shows the mixture idea on ARC-type grids but cannot answer gap 1. Still the only ARC-type multi-hypothesis item found.

source: Chen, Lin, Yuan, Zou, He, Goyal, Ong, Liu (2026) HypoSpace: set-valued hypothesis generation under underdetermination
finding: Gap 1. Asks LLMs to sample the full set of valid explanations. Models show high validity but poor coverage (mode collapse): they repeat the same few explanations as the space grows.
numbers: Three domains (causal graphs, 3D voxel gravity, Boolean genetic interactions); metrics Validity, Uniqueness, Recovery. Uniqueness and Recovery fall as the hypothesis space grows even when validity stays high. Exact table values not extracted this session.
limits: Numbers not recorded; I read the abstract and method text only. It measures generating explanations, not choosing among them.
agent_relevance: Asking one model for several frames gives near-duplicates. A forced diversity step (the rival must differ in a named cue) is needed for rival frames to be real.

source: Jo (2026) Committed Before Reasoning: answer pre-commitment in an open-weight LLM
finding: Gap 9. A one-premise trap (car wash 100 m away: walk or drive) shows the model fixing the answer before the reasoning and then arguing for it. Longer thinking does not repair it.
numbers: Qwen3-8B, 210 rollouts across 5 system prompts: wrong 'walk' in 85-100% of sampled rollouts and 100% of greedy rollouts, in thinking and non-thinking mode; a 4,096-token thinking budget still gave 85-100%. Activation read-out of 'walk' before the answer: 68% vs 17% neutral baseline. Same oracle: open question 2/16 vs closed question 11/16 on a positive control.
limits: Single small model, single probe item; activation oracle brittle. Preprint.
agent_relevance: Plausibility-driven stopping (the answer feels right, the reasoning is advocacy) shows in logs as a conclusion that precedes the premise check. A code check that the stated premises are actually used would separate it from check-based stopping.

source: Tack, Laban, Neville (2026) LLMs Get Lost in Evolving User Intent
finding: Gap 10. Code and tool tasks (SWE-Bench Verified, BIRD-SQL and others) turned into conversations where the user revises intent. Frontier models degrade after six intent transitions, and degradation grows with the number of transitions.
numbers: Four datasets including SWE-Bench Verified and BIRD-SQL (100 samples); six transitions per Evolve conversation (up to 7 turns); degradation up to roughly 30% from single-turn accuracy in the main tables; GPT 5.1/5.2/5.5 and Kimi tested; function switches are the hardest transition.
limits: I read the abstract, intro and table captions; per-model cells were not recorded. Preprint.
agent_relevance: A code-setting test of revision tracking. Old state and old tool results act as distractors, the same pattern as sensemaking residue.

source: Luo, Liu, Liu, Gong, Guo (2026) Multi-Turn Reasoning When Context Arrives in Pieces: Scalable Sharding and Memory-Augmented RL
finding: Gap 3. A trained rolling memory buffer (rewritten each turn) beats carrying full history, even when the full history is available at test time. A learned analogue of a cue ledger.
numbers: Abstract: Lost-in-Conversation loss up to 65%; trained on sharded GSM8K only; Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B-Instruct and Qwen3-4B; gains also on harder math and out-of-domain long-context QA (cell values not recorded).
limits: Requires RL training, which our agent cannot do. Small models, math.
agent_relevance: Supports the ledger idea in direction, but the mechanism is trained, not scaffolded.

source: Bruner and Potter (1964) Interference in visual recognition. Science
finding: Gap 6. Abstract opened. Pictures coming slowly into focus were recognised later when viewers first saw them very blurred. The longer the initial blur, the slower the recognition.
numbers: Sample sizes and effect sizes are not in the abstract and were not available.
quote: Interference may be accounted for partly by the difficulty of rejecting incorrect hypotheses based on substandard cues.
limits: Abstract only; no N, no effect size; replication record not checked.
agent_relevance: Early hypotheses from poor cues are hard to drop. Classic basis for 'form frames late', but it is a perception task.

source: Lord, Lepper, Preston (1984) Considering the opposite: a corrective strategy for social judgment. J Pers Soc Psychol
finding: Gap 6, 4. Abstract opened. Instructing people to consider the opposite reduced biased assimilation of evidence and biased hypothesis testing more than 'be fair and unbiased' instructions did.
numbers: Two experiments (social-issue evidence; personality-impression hypothesis testing). Sample sizes and effect sizes are not in the abstract.
limits: Abstract only. Later replications were not opened.
agent_relevance: Supports a code-forced 'what would the rival frame predict' step over a generic 'be careful' instruction.

source: Tolcott, Marvin, Lehner (1989) Expert decision-making in evolving situations; Lehner et al. (2008) Confirmation bias in complex analyses
finding: Gap 6. Bibliographic records only. Full texts and abstracts were behind paywalls or blocked (IEEE page empty, DTIC 403, Semantic Scholar abstract withheld). Tolcott et al. has 52 citations in Semantic Scholar.
numbers: No sample sizes or effect sizes retrieved.
limits: Not read. Findings in the earlier evidence files stay secondhand.
agent_relevance: None beyond what the earlier files already report.

source: Klein, Moon, Hoffman (2006) Making Sense of Sensemaking 2: A Macrocognitive Model. IEEE Intelligent Systems 21(5):88-92
finding: Gap 5. Existence and citation record confirmed through Crossref (authors Klein, Moon, Hoffman; 395 citing works). Full text and abstract could not be opened: ResearchGate 403, guessed IHMC and training-site copies 404, Crossref has no abstract. The 2007 chapter (Klein, Phillips, Rall, Peluso) was not found in any open source this session.
numbers: None.
limits: Bibliographic metadata only; opened is false because no text of the paper was read.
agent_relevance: The founding statements (seven activities, up to three frames, anchor rule) stay secondhand. Mark them single-source.
